card.name: The verb have before 'effect' or 'impact'
card.fires_on: The verb 'had' or 'have' right after a subject, where the next words will be 'no effect' or 'an impact on'. Seen mostly in drug-interaction statements, also in general science writing.

modes.label: Drug interaction results
modes.description: 'Had' follows a co-administered drug or dose, leading into 'no (significant) effect on' a drug level or pharmacokinetics.
modes.example: Cimetidine (400 mg b.i.d.)<< had>> no effect on vardenafil bioavailability

modes.label: General science prose
modes.description: 'Have' or 'have an' follows a factor, leading into 'an effect' or 'a small impact' on something.
modes.example: each variant is thought to<< have>> only a small impact on height

card.writes: It makes words like effect and impact more likely as the next word, in English and Chinese.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a sentence is about to say that something had, or did not have, an effect on something else.
